screenplay.text:
SIPHO AND SIPHOKAZI

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise, with deliberately awkward formatting.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     EXT. HARBOUR -- DAWN                                    1

               A small fishing harbour on a wild coast. Grey water, grey
               sky, a single row of forty-year-old wooden fishing-boats
               knocking against a concrete jetty.

               On the jetty, a salt-and-pepper-bearded fisherman in a sea-
               green oilskin coils a rope into a perfect figure-of-eight.
               This is SIPHO (50s).

               Gulls wheel. A dog trots past with a fish-head in its mouth.
               Sipho does not look up.

         2     INT. BAIT SHOP                                          2

               A tin-roofed shack that smells of salt and diesel. Buckets
               of sardines on ice. A calendar from nineteen-ninety-
               something curls on the wall.

               SIPHOKAZI (17), in a school jersey two sizes too big, counts
               coins onto the counter. MAMA THEMBI (60s), the shop's owner,
               watches her over half-moon glasses.

                                     MAMA THEMBI
                         Your uncle knows you're here?

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         My uncle knows everything. He just
                         doesn't say it.

                                     MAMA THEMBI
                               (sliding a bucket across
                               the counter, then leaning
                               in close so nobody else
                               will hear)
                         Kazi. Is it true, what they say?
                         The university letter came?

               Siphokazi nods. She cannot stop the smile.

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         Cape Town. Marine science. I start
                         in February.

                                     MAMA THEMBI
                         And Sipho?

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         I haven't told him yet.

                                                            SMASH CUT TO:









                                                                       2.


         3     INT./EXT. SIPHO'S BAKKIE - MOVING - DAY                 3

               An old white pick-up truck rattles down a dirt road toward
               the sea. Sipho drives. Siphokazi rides beside him with the
               bucket of sardines between her feet and a battered notebook
               on her knees: the TIDE BOOK.

                                     SIPHO
                         You're reading your grandmother's
                         tide book again.

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         She wrote down every tide for
                         thirty-one years. Every storm.
                         Every good catch.

                                     SIPHO
                         She wrote down every time I was
                         late for supper.

               Siphokazi laughs. Sipho almost smiles. The bakkie hits a
               pothole and the sardines slosh.

                                     SIPHO (CONT'D)
                         Kazi. Whatever you're not telling
                         me, tell me on the boat.

         4A    EXT. OPEN SEA - DAY                                     4A

               The fishing boat NOMSA, blue paint peeling, rides long
               swells a mile offshore. Sipho hauls a line hand over hand.
               Siphokazi baits hooks with quick, practised fingers.

               On the horizon, a bruise-coloured bank of cloud is building,
               fast.

               Neither of them sees it yet.

         4B    INT. BOAT CABIN - CONTINUOUS                            4B

               A cramped wheelhouse. A compass, a crackling VHF RADIO, a
               photograph of an old woman taped above the wheel.

               The radio bursts into life.

                                     COASTGUARD (V.O.)
                         All vessels, all vessels. Gale
                         warning for the coast from Hole in
                         the Wall to the river mouth. Return
                         to harbour immediately.

               Sipho is at the wheel in a heartbeat. Siphokazi scrambles in
               behind him.


                                                            (CONTINUED)






                                                                       3.


               CONTINUED:

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         The tide's turning. If we go
                         straight in over the bar now, we'll
                         hit it on the ebb.

                                     SIPHO
                         I have crossed that bar a thousand
                         times.

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         Not at half-past-four on a spring
                         ebb in the teeth of a south-
                         westerly. Gogo wrote it down. Look.

               She holds the tide book open under his nose. He does not
               look.

               Outside, a wave slaps over the bow. A coil of rope slides
               toward the open stern.

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         NO! THE ROPE!

               She lunges out of the cabin.

         5     EXT. OPEN SEA - CONTINUOUS                              5

               Rain comes sideways. Siphokazi grabs the rope just before it
               goes over and hauls it back, soaked to the skin.

               Sipho brings the boat around, away from the harbour mouth,
               heading north along the coast.

         6     INT. BOAT CABIN - CONTINUOUS                            6

               Siphokazi stumbles back in, dripping. Sipho does not take
               his eyes off the water.

                                     SIPHO
                               (barely audible over the
                               storm, and not quite
                               looking at her)
                         Where does the book say?

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         The cove at Mngazana. Gogo
                         sheltered there in eighty-seven.

                                     SIPHO
                         Then read me the way in. Every
                         word.


                                                            (CONTINUED)






                                                                       4.


               CONTINUED:

                                                            MATCH CUT TO:

         7     EXT. MNGAZANA COVE - NIGHT                              7

               A sheltered bay under dark cliffs. The storm roars out at
               sea, but here the water is almost still.

               The Nomsa sits at anchor, a single lamp swinging in her
               wheelhouse.

               No one speaks. The rain eases. One by one, stars come out
               over the cliffs.

         8     INT. BOAT CABIN - NIGHT                                 8

               Lamplight. Uncle and niece sit shoulder to shoulder on the
               floor, wrapped in one blanket, sharing a flask of sweet tea.

                                     SIPHO
                         When were you going to tell me?

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                               (startled)
                         Tell you what?

                                     SIPHO
                         Mama Thembi has a loud voice and a
                         small shop.

               A long pause. Siphokazi looks down at the tide book.

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         I start in February. Marine
                         science. I'm going to study all of
                         this. The tides and the storms and
                         the fish. Properly. Not just in a
                         notebook.

                                     SIPHO
                         Your grandmother did it properly.
                         In a notebook.

                                     SIPHOKAZI
                         I know.

               He takes the tide book from her, gently. He turns to the
               last page with writing on it. Then to the first empty page
               after it. He hands it back, and a pencil.

                                     SIPHO
                         Then you had better keep writing.









                                                                       5.


         9     INT. SIPHO'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT                    9

               Weeks later. A small kitchen, a paraffin lamp. A packed
               suitcase stands by the door.

               On the table, the tide book lies open beside a university
               prospectus. The newest entry in the book is in a young, neat
               hand.

               Nobody is in the room. The lamp flickers.

         10    EXT. HARBOUR -- DAWN                                    10

               The same grey water. The same row of boats. Sipho coils a
               rope into a perfect figure-of-eight.

               He looks up at the horizon for a long moment. Then, from the
               pocket of his oilskin, he takes out a new notebook and a
               pencil, and writes the date.

                                                            CUT TO BLACK.
